title: Banana peanut butter protein smoothie
summary: Two minutes, one blender, 35 g of protein. The frozen banana is what makes it thick instead of watery.

ingredients.note: Freeze them when they go spotty. A fresh banana makes a thin smoothie.
Turns it from a drink into something that holds you until lunch.
Only if your protein powder is unflavoured.
Sounds wrong, makes the peanut butter taste like more of itself.

steps: Liquid into the blender first, then the powder, then everything solid on top. This order stops the protein caking against the blades.
Too thick, add milk a splash at a time. Too thin, add a few ice cubes or more frozen banana and blend again.
tips: Blending the protein powder for too long makes it foamy and strangely sweet. Short and hard is better.
No frozen banana? Use a fresh one plus 4-5 ice cubes. Not as creamy, still fine.
Prep bags: banana chunks, oats and chia in a freezer bag. Tip the bag in, add milk and powder, blend.
health_notes: Real food carbs and 35 g of protein makes this a proper post-workout meal rather than a dessert. Skip the date and use unsweetened milk and there is no added sugar at all.

source.adapted: Basic gym smoothie, with the fruit-juice base swapped out for milk so it is not a sugar bomb.
